text:
alex: FYI perf CI alert just popped for the small-batch benchmark, p99 jumped ~12% in the late run. tagging for triage :eyes:
ci-bot: PERF ALERT | suite=small_batch_infer | p99 +12% | baseline=82ms current=92ms | run=1805009800 | link: https://ci.internal/runs/1805009800
mina: thanks alex. is this the nightly image or a PR run?
ci-bot: run_type=nightly-image | image=redwood/runtime:2026-02-15-b9c | tests=small_batch_infer,large_batch_smoke
joel: @mina @ryan I can take an initial look. grabbing the CI logs now. can someone drop the failing command?
ci-bot: failing_cmd: `./bench --suite small_batch_infer --concurrency 8 --seq 1024 --profile p99`
joel: ran that locally against the same image — I see a tail of longer host-to-device memcpy at iteration ~420. putting a quick trace on the bench.
ryan: I merged a tiny change to the KV cache allocator yesterday (PR #4122) but it was feature-gated behind env ENABLE_NEW_KV=false. CI image shouldn't have it on, unless image build picked up a different commit.
sara-r: ops noticed an image rebuild at 01:20 that included a new runtime tag. possible accidental canary merge. ops-qa, do you still have the build diffs?
ops-qa: pulling diffs now. build 2026-02-15-b9c includes: runtime: bump deps, hotfix for cuda kernel selection, and tooling:buildscript. the commit list: a3f2..b9c.
joel: kernel selection hotfix could explain different kernel choices under short sequences. I want a perf profile, sending a repro script to the CI team.
mina: plan: (1) @joel reproduce + profile, (2) if repo points to new kernel, bisect kernel selection change, (3) if not, ask infra to rebuild the image without the hotfix and rerun. anyone object?
ryan: no objections. I can run a quick bisect on kernel-selection config tomorrow morning if joel confirms it's implicated.
joel: quick profile snippet:
```
$ perf record -g -- ./bench --suite small_batch_infer --concurrency 8 --seq 1024 --iterations 1000
$ perf report --no-children | head -n 40
```
joel: initial flame shows heavy time in `cudaMemcpyAsync` plus unexpected lock contention in allocator. saving flame to /tmp/flame-1805009876.svg
sara-r: tagging infra: @ops-qa can you trigger a rebuild of the nightly image without the kernel-selection patch and queue just the small_batch_infer job? we need a clean diff. :pray:
ops-qa: queued rebuild as `redwood/runtime:2026-02-15-b9c-ctrl` and scheduled small_batch_infer run (job 1805012200). ETA ~12m.
mina: good. if the control run passes, we narrow to the image patch. if it fails, the regression is likely elsewhere.
joel: I'll start a bisect plan in #eng-runtime-bisect with steps. reassigning to @ryan for kernel bisect if control shows improvement.
ryan: acknowledged, will stand by. if needed I'll run `git bisect` across `kernel-selection` commits and test locally with the repro harness.
alex: can someone drop a quick corr report for PMs? they asked for customer-impact triage notes in case this hits production.
mina: I'll draft a short note after we have the control run. for now: severity=medium, impact=CI perf/regression detection only.
joel: control run results: job 1805012200 finished — p99=83ms (within baseline). copying logs: https://ci.internal/runs/1805012200/logs
joel: conclusion: image patch is likely cause. I'll start the bisect across the commits included in that build and update here.
ryan: thanks. I'll prepare a rollback patch candidate for the kernel-selection change in case the bisect narrows it down.
sara-r: great coordination team — add any rollback PRs to the ops queue and ping infra once ready. :thumbsup:
mina: closing loop: I'll update the incident tracker and mark as in-progress. will re-open if bisect points elsewhere.
alex: hugely appreciated everyone. :rocket:
